hard.simple_explanation: Treating a person or group unfairly because of who they are or what they believe.
hard.funny_explanation: When someone treats you like a rotten apple just because they don't like the color of your peel, even though you're perfectly sweet inside.

examples.text: Laws were passed to prevent discrimination against people with disabilities.
Refusing to give the cat a treat while the dog gets three is a clear case of feline discrimination!

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a teacher only letting students wearing blue shirts go to recess, which is totally unfair to everyone else.

words.meaning: Something that happens often or is usual.
A social class based on birth in society.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Explains how internal social divisions exist even within the same religion.
hard.simple_explanation: A social system that divides people into different groups based on their birth or family line.
hard.funny_explanation: An old-school social ladder where someone decided which rung you sit on before you were even born.

examples.text: The caste system has historically influenced social interactions in many parts of India.
If schools had a caste system, the 'Cool Kids' and the 'Math Geeks' would never be allowed to share a lunch table!

hard.real_world_analogy: Like being assigned a permanent character class in a game (Mage, Warrior, Rogue) that you can never change, no matter how much XP you get.

words.meaning: A small group within a larger religious group.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to show that even within one religion, smaller groups can have very different views.
hard.simple_explanation: A smaller group of people within a larger religious or political group who have slightly different beliefs.
hard.funny_explanation: Like a group of pizza lovers who all agree pizza is great, but split into 'sects' over whether pineapple belongs on it.

examples.text: Though they shared the same religion, they belonged to a different sect with unique rituals.
The 'Hidden-Chocolate-Eaters' is a secret sect within my family that my mom doesn't know about.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like different fan clubs for the same movie franchise—everyone loves Star Wars, but some only like the original movies.

words.meaning: Something that can happen or be done.
A group of people related to each other.
Many times or on many occasions.
Having a strong relationship with another person.

medium.funny_explanation: How you get along with others—ranging from 'best friends forever' to 'we pretend we don't see each other at the store.'

My relations with my alarm clock are currently very tense.

words.meaning: For this reason or as a result.

medium.funny_explanation: The word you use in an essay when you want to sound 50% smarter than you actually feel.

I forgot to charge my phone; thus, I had to actually look at people on the bus.

words.meaning: Who a person is and what they represent.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The central theme of the page: how people define themselves through various social groups.
hard.simple_explanation: The qualities, beliefs, and groups that make a person who they are.
hard.funny_explanation: The giant sticker collection of 'Who I Am' that you wear on your soul.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a social media profile bio that lists all your interests and where you're from.

words.meaning: The situations where something happens or exists.

Running is great in the context of a race, but weird in the context of a library.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like wearing a swimsuit—it's perfect at the pool (one context), but super awkward at a funeral (another context).

words.meaning: One thing covering part of another thing.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this to describe how multiple social disadvantages pile on top of each other, like being both poor and from a marginalized group.

examples.text: The overlapping interests of the two clubs led them to host a joint event.
My nap time and my math class are overlapping, which is a major problem for my dreams!

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a Venn diagram where the middle shaded part keeps getting bigger and bigger because more circles are moving into the same spot.

words.meaning: Groups in society being separated from each other.

medium.simple_explanation: When groups in a society split apart because of differences like wealth, race, or religion.

examples.text: Deep social division can make it hard for a country to stay united.
The great social division of the 8th grade started when half the class decided TikTok was 'cringe'.

words.meaning: A way in which people are not same.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It highlights the unfair treatment faced by specific social groups like Blacks in the US or Dalits in India based on their identity.
hard.simple_explanation: Treating a person or group unfairly because of who they are.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like a teacher giving everyone a gold star except for kids who wear green socks, even though the green-sock kids did the best work.

words.meaning: People who do not own any land.
Unfair treatment of people based on their background.

words.meaning: A situation that is not fair or right.

examples.text: Many people march in the streets to fight against social injustice.
It is a total injustice that my brother got a bigger slice of cake just because he's older.

words.meaning: How things are at a certain time.
Something that has a lot of value.
Groups of people with the same interests.

hard.funny_explanation: Think of a pizza cut into triangles but then someone cuts it in squares across the triangles—now everyone has a piece of both toppings!

Our love for video games cross-cuts our rivalry in football, so we are still friends after the match.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a school where the 'Cool Kids' and 'Nerds' are mixed up across different sports teams, so they can't just stay in two separate angry groups.

words.meaning: To put one group in a fight against another.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It is used to describe the act of setting two groups in competition or conflict with each other.

hard.funny_explanation: It sounds like a peach stone, but it's actually like a puppet master making two dolls have a pretend sword fight.

examples.text: Social divisions can pit one community against another if not managed well.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a boxing promoter who arranges for two heavyweights to fight in a ring.

words.meaning: Goals or needs shared by many people.

The cat and the dog shared a common interest: making sure the human dropped a piece of ham.

medium.funny_explanation: Think of a neighborhood where being a fan of one team means you automatically can't be friends with fans of the other team.

examples.text: The textbook uses Northern Ireland as an example of overlapping social differences.

words.meaning: A country where social differences do not clash.

medium.simple_explanation: A country in Europe where social differences 'cross-cut,' meaning people from different religions often have similar wealth levels.
medium.funny_explanation: The land of windmills, tulips, and people who figured out how to disagree without starting a food fight.

examples.text: In the Netherlands, religious differences don't lead to as much conflict as in other places.
I want to visit the Netherlands just to see if everyone actually wears wooden shoes while being nice to each other.

words.meaning: Mostly or mainly consisting of one thing.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The text uses this to state that Northern Ireland and the Netherlands are 'mostly' or 'largely' Christian.
hard.simple_explanation: Mainly, mostly, or for the most part.
hard.funny_explanation: If a pizza is predominantly pepperoni, you'll have to go on a treasure hunt just to find a single mushroom.

My diet is predominantly chocolate, which my dentist says is 'predominantly bad' for my teeth.

words.meaning: Separated into different parts or groups.

medium.simple_explanation: Members of the Roman Catholic Church, which is a major branch of Christianity.
medium.funny_explanation: A group of Christians who follow the Pope and have been around for a very, very long time.

examples.text: Catholics and Protestants are the two main religious groups mentioned in the text.
My Catholic grandma can finish a rosary faster than I can finish a bag of chips.

words.meaning: Another large group within the Christian religion.

medium.simple_explanation: Members of various Christian churches that are separate from the Roman Catholic Church.
medium.funny_explanation: A branch of Christianity that started when people decided they wanted to do things a bit differently than the Catholics.

Protestants come in so many varieties it's like a buffet of different church styles.

examples.text: Overlapping differences can often lead to violent conflicts in a country.
The conflict between my dog and the mailman is legendary in this neighborhood.

words.meaning: Things that have a chance of happening.

words.meaning: Feelings of anger or worry between groups.

medium.funny_explanation: It's that awkward silence in the room right after someone says something they definitely shouldn't have.

There were high tensions in the kitchen when Mom found out someone ate the hidden cookies.

words.meaning: To find a way for different groups to live together.

hard.simple_explanation: To make fit, adjust to, or provide space for someone's needs.
hard.funny_explanation: It's like scooting over on the sofa so your giant dog can sit down too—you're making room for him!

examples.text: A democratic government tries to accommodate the needs of all its citizens.
The hotel was able to accommodate my request for a room shaped like a giant pineapple.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a multi-plug adapter that allows different types of electronics to all plug into the same wall socket.

words.meaning: To be present or to live.
Extremely big or huge in size.

medium.simple_explanation: A small country in Europe known for having multiple communities that speak different languages.
medium.funny_explanation: A tiny country that is world-famous for chocolate, waffles, and having a lot of complicated political meetings.

examples.text: Belgium is a small country with many different social communities.
If I lived in Belgium, I would probably spend all my time eating waffles and learning three languages.

words.meaning: A country that is changing due to new people.

medium.simple_explanation: A large country in Central Europe that was once very similar in culture but is now becoming more diverse.
medium.funny_explanation: The place where they make fast cars, great bread, and used to have everyone looking pretty much the same.

examples.text: Germany is undergoing change as people from other parts of the world move there.
Germany is great until you realize they have about 500 words for different types of sausages.

words.meaning: A country that used to be very similar.

medium.simple_explanation: A Northern European country known for its social equality and changing population.
medium.funny_explanation: The home of IKEA, meatballs, and people who are very polite but also very private.

examples.text: Even countries like Sweden are becoming more multi-cultural due to migration.
In Sweden, it's so cold that even the snowmen probably want to move to India.

words.meaning: A society where everyone is very similar.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: This describes societies like Germany or Sweden in the past, where people were very similar to each other.
hard.simple_explanation: Consisting of parts or people that are all of the same kind.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of a pack of classic yellow tennis balls—they are all the same color, same fuzziness, and same bounce. That's a homogeneous pack!

examples.text: The village had a homogeneous population where everyone shared the same culture.
My sock drawer is finally homogeneous; I threw away all the neon ones and kept only the boring grey ones.

hard.real_world_analogy: A bowl of plain vanilla ice cream with nothing else in it—it's the same flavor all the way through.

words.meaning: Experiencing a change or a process.

medium.simple_explanation: Experiencing or going through a specific process or change.
medium.funny_explanation: It's like when your bedroom is undergoing a 'renovation,' which is just a fancy word for it being a giant mess right now.

examples.text: The city is undergoing many changes to improve the public transport system.
My brain is undergoing a total meltdown trying to remember these vocabulary words.

words.meaning: Happening in a very fast way.
A large number of people arriving at once.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: It describes the rapid arrival of many people from other parts of the world into a country.
hard.simple_explanation: An arrival or entry of large numbers of people or things.
hard.funny_explanation: It's what happens when the school bell rings for lunch and 500 hungry kids suddenly rush into the cafeteria at once.

examples.text: The city saw a massive influx of tourists during the summer festival.
There was a sudden influx of ants in the kitchen after I dropped my lollypop.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like water rushing into a bathtub when you turn the tap on full blast.

words.meaning: People who move to a new country for work.

medium.funny_explanation: Basically, human birds who fly to a new place to find better worms (jobs) and build a new nest.

examples.text: Migrants bring their unique cultures and traditions to their new countries.
I am a migrant every morning when I move from my warm bed to the cold kitchen.

words.meaning: The habits and beliefs of a group.
A group of people with shared social bonds.

medium.simple_explanation: A group of people who live together or share similar backgrounds and interests.
medium.funny_explanation: Like your group chat, but in real life, where everyone actually lives near each other and shares stuff.

words.meaning: Having many different cultures in one society.

examples.text: Most countries today are multi-cultural because of people moving around the world.

words.meaning: Large or important enough to be noticed.

There was a significant change in my mood once I realized it was Friday.

hard.funny_explanation: It’s like being part of a big global family tree where everyone shares the same secret recipes and cool dance moves.

examples.text: The festival celebrated the various ethnic groups living in the city.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like different 'chapters' of a book club where each group reads different types of books based on where they grew up.

medium.funny_explanation: Anything that has to do with how much cash is in your pocket and why a candy bar costs more than it used to.

examples.text: People often move to other countries in search of better economic opportunities.
My economic status is currently 'broke' until I finish my chores and get my allowance.

words.meaning: Chances to do something better or new.

medium.funny_explanation: Like finding a golden ticket in a chocolate bar—it’s your big chance to do something cool!

examples.text: Education provides many opportunities for young people to succeed.
I never miss opportunities to nap, especially when I'm supposed to be cleaning my room.

words.meaning: Writing that uses rhythm to share feelings.

words.meaning: System where people vote to choose their leaders.

examples.text: Competition among parties tends to divide the people in a society.

hard.funny_explanation: Think of a giant Lego castle that loses its 'glue' and turns back into a pile of random bricks on the floor.

examples.text: Political conflict can lead to the disintegration of a nation's unity.

medium.funny_explanation: Like the face you make when you accidentally drink unsweetened coffee thinking it was hot cocoa.

words.meaning: Smaller groups within a larger religious group.

words.meaning: People belonging to the Roman Catholic Church.

medium.funny_explanation: One of the oldest religious groups around, known for beautiful churches and a leader with a very impressive hat.

I represented all the students who wanted longer lunch breaks during the school meeting.

words.meaning: Brought together to act as one single unit.

examples.text: Three factors determine the outcomes of social politics.
The outcome of my cooking experiment was a very smokey kitchen.

words.meaning: To produce a change in something.
Feelings of anger or lack of trust.

medium.funny_explanation: That awkward, heavy feeling in a room when two people have just had a big argument

examples.text: Social differences can create deep divisions and tensions.
The tensions in the room rose when I accidentally ate my sister's hidden chocolate.

words.meaning: Managing or handling a task or situation.
Related to people living together in groups.
Splitting people into groups based on differences.

medium.simple_explanation: The groups or splits that happen in a society based on things like religion or wealth
medium.funny_explanation: Think of a pizza cut into slices—except the slices are groups of people who can't agree on whether pineapple belongs on top.

examples.text: The government tried to bridge the divisions between the two groups.
The cafeteria had clear divisions: the jocks, the nerds, and the kids who try to balance spoons on their noses.

words.meaning: Things that are said or written clearly.

medium.funny_explanation: That magical moment when your answer matches the one in the back of the book.

words.meaning: A system where people vote for their leaders.

medium.funny_explanation: A giant group project where everyone actually gets to vote on who does the work and what the grade should be.

examples.text: In a democracy, every citizen has a voice in how the country is run.
My family isn't a democracy; my mom is the president, the judge, and the person who decides when it's bedtime.

words.meaning: A situation where people try to win something.

medium.simple_explanation: A situation where different people or groups try to be more successful than others
medium.funny_explanation: Like a race where everyone is trying to get the last slice of cake, but with political votes instead of frosting.

examples.text: Political competition can sometimes cause tension between different social groups.
There is a fierce competition between my brother and me to see who can take the longest shower.

words.meaning: Shown clearly in a particular way.
Groups of people with shared interests or homes.

medium.simple_explanation: Groups of people who live in the same area or share common interests and goals
medium.funny_explanation: Your 'squad' or the group of people you'd trust to watch your dog or share your snacks.

examples.text: Different communities should be able to express their needs peacefully.
The gaming community is great until you accidentally delete someone's high score.

words.meaning: To speak out or express an opinion.
Complaints about being treated unfairly.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this word to show that democracy provides a platform for groups to voice their complaints and issues.
hard.simple_explanation: Formal complaints or feelings of resentment about being treated unfairly.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'Official List of Grumbles' you write down when your brother gets the bigger half of the chocolate bar.

examples.text: The students presented their grievances about the long homework hours to the principal.
My cat has many grievances, mostly involving the empty spot in the middle of his food bowl.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a suggestion box in a cafeteria where students can report if the soup is too salty.

words.meaning: The specific way in which something happens.
To make space or adjust for someone's needs.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Introduced to describe how democracy manages to fit in and respect various social differences.

hard.funny_explanation: Being a super-flexible host who finds a bed for a friend, a basket for a dog, and a shelf for a pet rock.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a teacher moving desks around so that everyone in the class can see the board clearly.

words.meaning: Having many different types of people or things.

hard.funny_explanation: The tragic moment when your giant sandcastle gets hit by a wave and turns into a flat puddle of mush.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like a jigsaw puzzle that falls off the table and scatters into a hundred disconnected pieces.

words.meaning: A group of people living together in one area.

words.meaning: More than one of something.

I have multiple excuses for why my homework isn't done, but the dog-ate-it one is a classic.

words.meaning: The qualities that make a person who they are.

In online games, people can have secret identities that are way cooler than their real ones.

words.meaning: The order in which things follow each other.

medium.funny_explanation: Being the person who cheers the loudest when your friend finally lands a kickflip.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like one of the many different sections of a giant global family tree.

hard.funny_explanation: The 'Rebel Christians' who decided a few centuries ago that they wanted to do things a bit differently.

medium.funny_explanation: That feeling you get when a song is so good it makes your soul want to do a happy dance.

My connection to nature is very spiritual until a mosquito decides to bite me.

hard.real_world_analogy: Like the sun, which is the ultimate source of power for everything on our planet.
